scope: Protect authored and legacy relative /media/<asset-id> references in renderer-supported page content; cover image, card, gallery, video poster and legacy video/audio sources, and avoid successful-run screenshot artifact storage.; authored versioned Video/Audio src coverage added locally after finding the earlier regression exercised legacy nodes only.; regression coverage now separately verifies authored and structured Carousel URL source paths, archive protection, and exact-byte public delivery. Latest follow-up: the scanner now delegates URL acceptance to the exact renderer safeMediaUrl validator before pathname parsing, preventing malformed backslash paths from being normalized into public media grants while retaining renderer-accepted whitespace normalization.

finding.reproduction: The public renderer accepts safe internal URL values in versioned authored image/video/audio sources, video posters, normalized Card imageSrc, authored Gallery/Carousel item src, and normalized structured Gallery/Carousel item src. The reference scan only matched explicit assetId fields. A published internal URL could therefore be omitted from usage/archive checks and public media authorization. The legacy sanci-document adapter also renders contentVersion-free image.src, video/audio.src, and video.poster values; the first authored-only pass missed that renderer path. The latest regression isolated both directions: leading/trailing control whitespace accepted by safeMediaUrl must remain discoverable, while a trailing backslash that WHATWG URL normalizes into a slash must not be counted as renderer-valid or grant the public route.
finding.fix: Recognize only an exact relative /media/<MEDIA_ASSET_ID> pathname (allowing the renderer's trailing slash normalization and query string). Apply renderer-specific version, node type, media MIME, Media Library ID override, Card normalization, Gallery/Carousel 40-item bounds, and normalized structured-content checks before a URL-backed reference authorizes public access. The exact URL authorizer now accepts both authored v1 and metadata-free legacy media nodes while preserving MIME and Media Library ID precedence. publicMediaUrlAssetId now calls safeMediaUrl first, rejects non-relative/protocol-relative/backslash-rooted normalized values, then checks the exact /media/<asset-id> pathname.
regressions: A published model containing direct image src, Card imageSrc, authored Gallery items[0].src, structured Gallery contentModel.items[0].src, and video poster URLs reports all five references.
An active internal URL reference prevents media archival with HTTP 409.
The published media route returns the exact local R2 fixture bytes for a referenced internal URL.
Editor screenshots upload only after the complete Editor Core job fails, after every required check, with a 7-day retention window.
The active-plan audit continues to upload only its bounded text artifact with a 30-day retention window.
A legacy sanci-document Image src and Video poster remain visible usage references and authorize the exact local fixture bytes; a Media Library ID override continues to deny the stale URL.
Legacy sanci-document Video src and Audio src internal URLs are reported by usage, block archive with HTTP 409, and authorize exact matching local WebM/WAV fixture bytes.

A distinct authored v1 WebM Video src and WAV Audio src at /media/{id} each appear in usage, block archival with HTTP 409, and authorize exact matching fixture bytes; distinct bytes isolate the authored assertions from content-addressed deduplication.

Authored Carousel props.items[0].src and structured Carousel props.contentModel.items[0].src each resolve as distinct image references, appear in site-scoped usage by exact node/path, block archive with HTTP 409, and authorize only matching local PNG fixture bytes.
Renderer-normalized whitespace around a relative /media/<id> is included in usage, served as exact matching bytes, and blocks archive with 409.
A malformed trailing-backslash /media/<id> rejected by the renderer is excluded from usage and returns 404 on the published route; URL parser normalization cannot invent a public authorization.
